title: Tadd Dameron
summary: Gordon cannot name Dameron's ballad but describes him as cool, introspective, professorial and his music like him.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: That seemed to be a group with Ike Quebec, and then he brought in Art Blakey, and then Tadd Dameron came into the fold as well to record.

Oh, Tadd! Tadd Dameron. These names are so beautiful to me. Each one of them was so great in their own way. Each one was representative of their own art. Tadd was a great arranger and wrote gorgeous songs. What was that gorgeous song he wrote... Oh, it’s so gorgeous I can’t... I know it when I hear it.
“On A Misty Night”? Is that it?

“Our Delight” is an upper tune. No, one ballad. But when I hear it (and they always play it), I say, “All right, Tadd.” Anyway, there’s so much music that went by my ears, it’s hard to extract it all. But the names bring back a flood of memories of how great these artists were.
[THE TUNE IS PROBABLY “IF YOU COULD SEE ME NOW”]
What was he like as a person, Tadd?

Tadd. Well, he was a very round-faced man. He had very short-cropped hair, I remember. Very...mmm...caramel-colored skin, and very sweet. He was very introspective. You didn’t get a slap on the back or a hug from him. He was cool. I guess he’s one of the first cool musicians I really got to know a little bit. And very serious and deep-thinking. Professorial, I would say. That’s how I got to know him. That was his persona to me. And his music was very much like him. It was cool, and very original, and very personal. That was Tadd Dameron. “Our Delight,” yeah, I remember that. I loved that name. It sounds like candy.
